steps.name: QC, VST normalization, and variance structure
caveats: Salmon counts with unknown length correction: DESeq2 handles uncorrected counts; do not apply a second length normalization on top
If a few genes dominate (e.g., hemoglobin), they are a real blood signal — keep them and let the variance ranking decide
Whole-blood data is dominated by immune-cell composition; note this in the report rather than filtering it away
steps.context: Raw gene-level Salmon counts, 12000 genes x 120 samples, one CSV with a gene ID column. Unpaired case/control cohort, single batch. Metadata has only sample IDs and condition, so no covariate adjustment beyond condition is possible.
steps.question: Are the 120 samples of comparable quality, and how much of the expression variance is already explained by the known case-vs-control label?
steps.description: Load counts.csv (12000 x 121, first column gene IDs) and metadata.csv (120 x 2). Verify sample ID alignment between the two files. Filter genes with negligible counts, run DESeq2 VST normalization on raw Salmon gene counts (standard practice when the delivered counts have not been length-corrected; state this assumption), compute library-size summaries, PCA on the VST matrix, sample-sample Pearson and Euclidean distance matrices, and report the variance explained by condition on the leading PCs plus an MDS/t-SNE view. Flag, but do not silently drop, outlier samples (large z-scored distance to all others).
acceptance_criteria: VST-normalized matrix and a filtered count matrix are written with a documented gene-filter rule (e.g., counts > threshold in N samples)
PCA and sample-distance QC outputs exist; the fraction of variance on PC1-PC5 explained by condition is reported
A stated outlier policy (flag, and exclude only with a written rationale) is recorded before any clustering step runs

steps.name: Consensus clustering across k, views, and distances
caveats: Consensus clustering overfits to regularity; the shortlist is a candidate list, not a conclusion — T2S2 decides
Clustering on all 12000 genes dilutes signal; do not cluster on the full matrix
Feature selection uses all samples — this is unsupervised by design, but the same genes must be fixed once and reused in T2S2 resampling
steps.context: T1S1 produces a VST matrix (12000 genes x 120 samples) and a condition-adjusted variant. ConsensusClusterPlus is available in R; use item subsampling rather than gene resampling, and record the seed for reproducibility.
steps.question: How many reproducible clusters (k) do the 120 samples support beyond the case/control split, in the full data and after removing the condition signal?
steps.description: Select the top 1000-2000 most variable genes from the VST matrix. Run ConsensusClusterPlus for k=2..8 (>=500 resampling iterations, 80% item subsampling) on two feature views — VST values, and VST residuals after regressing out condition — and two distances (1 - Pearson correlation, Euclidean on scaled features). Also run a reduced PC-space variant (top 30-50 PCs) as a third view to check that k choices are not artifacts of noisy genes. Produce consensus matrices, CDF and delta-area plots, PAC (proportion of ambiguous clustering) per k, mean silhouette per k, and a shortlist of candidate k values with justification.
acceptance_criteria: Consensus matrices, CDF plots, delta-area and PAC values are produced for every k in 2..8, for both feature views and both distances
A ranked shortlist of candidate k values with their PAC/silhouette scores is written
The same pipeline is applied to the condition-adjusted view, and whether the shortlist changes is reported explicitly

steps.name: Stability, permutation null, and relation to condition
caveats: Jaccard for a cluster absent in a resample is defined as 0; state the convention
Do not cherry-pick the seed; report the seeds used and keep them identical across candidate k comparisons
steps.context: Uses the consensus clustering configuration fixed in T2S1 (same genes, same distance, same seed policy). Permutation nulls are cheap here: 12000 genes x 120 samples shuffles in seconds, so >=100 permutations are affordable.
steps.question: Are the candidate partitions stable under resampling, better than what structureless data of the same shape produces, and distinct from the case/control label itself?
steps.description: For each candidate k from T2S1: (a) repeat clustering over >=100 subsamples (e.g., 80% of samples) and compute adjusted Rand index between each subsample solution and the full-data labels, plus cluster-wise Jaccard stability; (b) build a null by permuting each gene's values across samples (>=100 permutations), running the identical consensus-clustering configuration, and recording the null PAC distribution — observed PAC must be compared against this null; (c) compute ARI and a contingency table between the discovered clusters and the known case/control labels, and between clusters from the condition-adjusted view and the raw view; (d) deliver a verdict per candidate k: how many subgroups (if any) are supported, and with what stability.
acceptance_criteria: Per-candidate-k tables of subsample ARI distributions and cluster-wise Jaccard values exist
The permutation null (permuted matrix through the identical pipeline) yields a null PAC distribution, and observed-vs-null PAC comparisons are reported for every candidate k
ARI between the consensus labels and the condition label, plus a cluster x condition contingency table, are reported
A final verdict per candidate k: stable / unstable / equivalent-to-condition-label

steps.name: Subgroup characterization and marker genes
caveats: If the only stable partition is the condition label itself, this step reports that finding and characterizes the case-vs-control contrast instead
Markers from a data-driven split share information with the clustering; treat marker lists as descriptive, not independently validated
steps.context: Markers should be defined within condition strata if subgroup and condition are correlated, so markers describe the subgroup rather than the disease label.
steps.question: What do the (candidate) subgroups look like: are they aligned with or independent of case/control, and which genes mark them?
steps.description: For the verdict partition (or, if none is stable, for the best-supported candidate as an explicitly labeled exploratory view): crosstab clusters against case/control with a chi-square/permutation test; identify subgroup marker genes by DESeq2/edgeR contrasts of each cluster vs the rest (stratified by condition where clusters and condition overlap); annotate the PCA and a heatmap of top markers by both subgroup and condition.
acceptance_criteria: Cluster x condition crosstab with a permutation-based association test is written
Marker tables (log2FC, Wald p, BH-adjusted p per subgroup) exist for every stable subgroup
PCA and heatmap annotated by both subgroup and condition are produced

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of subgroup markers
caveats: Blood marker sets will pick up immune pathways heavily; report this as the known composition of whole blood, not as a subgroup-specific discovery, unless the pathway is differential between subgroups
Pathway results on an exploratory partition are hypothesis-generating only
steps.context: The WikiPathways human GMT under /mnt/refs is HGNC-symbol based, matching the gene symbols expected in a Salmon gene-level count matrix; verify symbol overlap before running and report the mapping rate. fgsea and clusterProfiler are both installed.
steps.question: Which human pathways characterize each subgroup's markers, giving the discovered (or candidate) subgroups biological context?
steps.description: Run GSEA/over-representation of each subgroup's ranked marker list against the WikiPathways human gene sets (GMT: one pathway per line, '%'-delimited descriptor, HGNC symbols) from the reference store. Report top pathways per subgroup with FDR. If no human pathway resource is present at run time, state that plainly and stop the step — no substitute mammalian GMT should be silently applied to human data.
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment results per subgroup marker set (pathway, NES or enrichment score, FDR) are written, or the report explicitly records that no human pathway resource was available in this environment
The same consequence class (up/down) is kept consistent between markers and gene-set analysis, and is documented

plan.title: Subgroup discovery and stability in 120-sample blood RNA-seq
plan.analytical_narrative: The cohort is 60 unpaired cases vs 60 controls (whole blood, human), profiled as 12000 gene-level Salmon counts x 120 samples in a single batch, with metadata carrying only the condition column. The question is whether unsupervised structure exists beyond the case/control split, in how many groups, and how reproducible it is. The logic is: (1) normalize the raw Salmon counts with a count model (DESeq2 VST), filter near-zero genes, and establish how much variance the known condition label explains so any 'new' structure is interpreted against it — including a condition-adjusted matrix so subgroups are not just rediscovering case vs control; (2) run consensus clustering (ConsensusClusterPlus) over k=2..8 on the most variable genes, with two feature views (VST and condition-adjusted) and two distance metrics, scoring candidate k by PAC, delta-area and silhouette; (3) test stability and reality of the partition: subsample/bootstrap re-clustering with ARI and cluster-wise Jaccard, a permutation null (gene-wise shuffling of the same matrix) to show the observed PAC/stability exceeds what structureless data of this shape produces, and the ARI/crosstab between discovered clusters and the condition label; (4) characterize any robust partition by its association with condition and by subgroup marker genes; (5) map those markers to WikiPathways human gene sets (provisioned under /mnt/refs) so the reported subgroups carry biological context, with a graceful outcome if the GMT is absent. Consensus clustering is known to detect regularity rather than only true subtypes, which is why the permutation null and subsample ARI are not optional extras but the deciding evidence.
